decisions.issues: v02 is clean and follows the correction. The background is now the Travancore coastal road: palms with pepper vines, laterite cliffs, sand and a hazy sea. There are no European buildings. Nagoji is on screen left on the small chestnut with the flaxen mane. Ibrahim is on screen right on the dark brown pony with the black mane, patting a bulging vest pocket and looking at Nagoji. His scar is on the correct (left) cheek, on the screen-right side of his face. Minor points: (1) Ibrahim's scar is a pinkish line, not fully pale, but it matches his sheet's detail. (2) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled to mid-forearm instead of reaching the bandaged wrists. The bandages cover his wrists and fingers are bare, which is acceptable. (3) Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging drop, not a stud. The open sky across the upper centre and right gives room for both Ibrahim balloons. v01 is rejected because it shows a European church and fort in the background.

v02 is acceptable and follows the correction. It is drawn in the inked line-and-wash style. It shows the still inlet with cargo boats and canoes, cooking smoke at right, the rough red laterite outer wall with a loopholed parapet, and the long tiled hall on dark pillars carved with coiling vines and tigers. The rampart runs up the higher ground behind with a Kerala-roofed watchtower. Every guard is a bare-chested Nair in a white mundu with a dark sash and topknot, holding a spear or matchlock. There are no helmets and no Europeans. Minor point: the plinth of one pillar near the right of the hall terrace (about x 0.81, y 0.41) has a tiny carved band. At 400% zoom its squiggles look faintly like glyphs; at print size it reads as ornament, so it is worth retouching only if desired. Ibrahim speaks from off panel, at the camera position on the road, so the tail points to the bottom edge. The open sky at upper left gives room for the balloon. v01 is rejected for a helmeted European-looking soldier and its photographic rendering.

v02 is acceptable and the edit worked. Ibrahim faces screen right and his visible right cheek is now unmarked. The gateway is built of rough red laterite blocks. The speaking Nair guard raises an open palm in three-quarter view with his mouth clear. Nagoji is in the foreground, bare-headed in his collarless cream shirt and dhoti, with bandaged hands, his head turned sharply toward the guards. The red flag carries a white conch. Notes: (1) Through the gate stands a whitewashed two-storey building with tiled roofs and a small tiled tower with finials. It reads as Kerala palace architecture (like Padmanabhapuram), not a church or fort. If the author finds it colonial-looking, paint it out to the open pillared hall. (2) Nagoji's sleeves are rolled up. (3) Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging drop. Lettering can go on the plain laterite wall at upper right (the guard's balloon, near his head) and in the sky at top centre (the caption). v01 is rejected because Ibrahim's scar is on his visible right cheek and the gate is pale grey dressed stone.

v02 is acceptable and follows the correction. The background is the hall compound: the tiled hall on carved dark pillars at left, the laterite outer wall, palms and the still inlet with small country boats. There is no European fort, church or ship. Nagoji's bandaged hand still rests on the flaxen mane while the horse tosses its head away toward the groom. The groom is a bare-chested Kerala stable hand with a topknot and white mundu, so he cannot be mistaken for Ibrahim. Minor points: (1) The horse is a medium red chestnut, not dark liver-chestnut, but it matches the horse picked for panel 1.2. (2) Only two digits of Nagoji's bandaged hand show; the rest are buried in the mane, which is plausible. (3) Faint stubble shading on Nagoji's chin, within tolerance. (4) Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging drop. There is wide clear sky across the top centre for the caption. v01 is rejected for a European fort and church on the headland, a European ship and a dockside crane.

v02 is acceptable. The edit fixed the far end and kept the rest. The shot is from behind at the top of the stone steps. Nagoji is bare-headed, with curly hair caught back, a long-sleeved cream shirt and dhoti, bandaged wrists, and a small gold stud and moustache tip in his partial profile. Ibrahim wears his white turban, teal short coat and striped shoulder cloth. The pillars are carved with vines and tigers, the rafters are dark and the floor has mats. Bare-chested, topknotted courtiers in white mundus sit either side of a clear lane, and the open side with the sea below is on screen left. At the far end, Varma sits cross-legged in the cream-and-gold turban with the peacock-feather crest, bare-chested, with the cloth over one shoulder and gold necklaces. His head is bowed over an unlettered map, so his eyes are hidden. Ramayyan, thin, balding and in white, sits at a low table on screen right. The red banner shows a silver conch with no lettering, the lamps are open-wick brass, and the incense wisp is gone. Minor points: Varma's face is only about 25 px wide, and a heavy jaw outline with chin shadow can suggest a faint beard line under magnification, but at reading size it reads as moustache and clean chin. The guards beside the banner have short beards and cross-straps, which is fine. The sky at upper left and the rafter band leave clean room for both captions. v01 remains unacceptable: the king is bare-headed with a topknot and bearded.

v02 fixes the staging. Nagoji is in clean profile facing screen left, with a thick curled moustache, a clean chin with light stubble, loose curly hair, a collarless cream shirt and bandaged forearms. Ibrahim leans in at right with his LEFT cheek to camera, and the scar runs on the correct side from ear to jaw through the beard. His hand rests well drawn on the bulging vest pocket, and there is no painted border. Three background faults remain. (1) The figure at the low table at the king's left hand, which Ibrahim's line 'And his diwan' points to, is drawn as an elder with a full white beard, full grey hair and a bordered shawl. He reads as a sage or priest, not Ramayyan (thin, clean-shaven, balding with curly black hair at the sides, plain white cloth). He contradicts 2.2 and the very next close-up in 2.4. (2) Varma looks straight out at the camera with his eyes showing, against the page note to withhold the king's eyes until page 3 (2.2 and 2.5 keep his gaze down). He also sits on a cushion above grey stone steps, not on a low wooden platform. (3) A crenellated, European-looking fort shows across the water through the open side. Lesser notes: Ibrahim's scar is a bright orange-red line. That is consistent in hue with his sheet, but brighter than the requested pale healed line. Nagoji's ear ornament is a gold disc hanging from a small stud (drop rather than stud; noted only, not a reason to reject). The left half of the hall uses pale stone columns rather than the dark carved wooden pillars of 2.1. The plain grey band at upper right and the sky at upper left suit the two balloons. v01 is still unacceptable: the scar is on Ibrahim's right cheek and the framing has a painted border.
decisions.correction: Keep this image exactly as it is: Nagoji in clean profile facing screen left with moustache, clean chin, loose curly hair, cream shirt and bandaged forearms; Ibrahim leaning in at right with his left cheek and its scar toward the camera, white turban, grey-flecked beard, teal coat and his hand on the bulging vest pocket; the bare-chested topknotted courtiers in white mundus; the red conch banner and brass lamps; the open side with the sea at the far left; and the plain sky and grey band at the top for two balloons. Change only these background details. (1) Replace the white-bearded elder at the low table at the king's left hand (screen right of the king) with Ramayyan, the diwan, matching panel 2.4. He is thin with sharp fine features and CLEAN-SHAVEN, with no beard and no white or grey hair. His crown is balding, with curly black hair at the sides. Plain white cloth wraps his upper body, with no bordered shawl and no jewellery, and he bends over unlettered palm-leaf bundles with a stylus. (2) Marthanda Varma keeps his cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, thick moustache, clean-shaven chin, bare chest, cream-and-gold shoulder cloth and gold necklaces. His head is bowed toward a map unrolled on the mat before him, so his eyes are hidden and he does not look toward the camera. He sits cross-legged on a mat on a low wooden platform, with no stone steps beneath it. (3) Through the open side at the far left, show only sea, palms and a green headland: no fort, castle, tower or crenellated wall. (4) Tone Ibrahim's scar down to a thin, muted pinkish-brown healed line in the same place, with no bright orange or glowing red.

decisions.issues: v02 does what the edit asked for. Varma's eyes are down on the map and one hand rests flat on it. The guards wear white head cloths and Ibrahim gestures in profile on screen left of Nagoji. v01 stays rejected: Varma has his chin on his hand and looks toward the camera, and one guard wears a red turban. Minor notes on v02: (1) A distant hill fort shows through the open side. It reads as Indian, not European, and matches neighbouring panel 3.3. (2) There are faint specks along the map's lower edge, too small to read as writing. (3) Nagoji is seen from behind, so his moustache, chin and ear ornament cannot be checked. His bow is a shallow dip of head and shoulders, which fits the script. (4) Lettering fits on the plain sunlit wall above Nagoji's head (x 0.26 to 0.52, y 0 to 0.2) and between the banners above Varma.

v02 fixes the setting. It now shows the coastal hall from panel 3.4: dark carved pillar, palms and sea through the open side, a brass lamp with open wicks, the grey wall with its frieze band, the platform step, a polished floor and a mat. Nagoji wears a plain long-sleeved cream shirt over a white dhoti with no sash. The sleeves cover his wrists and the linen wrappings are clean. Varma's bare forearm, gold bangle and gold-bordered cream cloth enter from the left, and only his index and middle fingers are extended (thumb on top, ring and little fingers curled). v01 stays rejected: it is set in a prison cell with a barred window, a wall ring and chain, and gives Nagoji a red sash. Minor notes on v02: (1) Nagoji's wrapped hands hang loosely together in front of his body rather than strictly at his sides, but they are still and at the far edge of frame as the script asks. (2) Varma's two fingers are spread slightly, but they clearly point down at Nagoji's hands. (3) No faces are in frame. Both speakers are off-panel above: Ramayyan's tail goes to the top edge at centre, Nagoji's to the top edge above his body. (4) Clear plain wall for both lines at x 0.33 to 0.78, y 0.02 to 0.33.

v02 follows the edit instruction. The dais, the carved chairs and the turbaned seated figures are gone. Behind Ramayyan there is only the closed wall, the conch-on-red banner and plain floor. The one courtier at far left is bare-chested in a white mundu with a topknot. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery, no sacred thread, profile toward the mat, pointing with the stylus, palm-leaf bundle at his hip. Nagoji has a thick curled moustache and clean chin. He is bare-headed, with hair half tied back, and wears a collarless cream shirt and dhoti with bandaged hands. He crouches stiffly onto the woven mat. The brass lamp has open wicks. There is no text. The sky at upper centre-right is clear for both of Ramayyan's balloons. Minor points: (1) The two guards wear white short-sleeved tunics with crossed belts, but the guards in 5.1 and 5.2 are bare-chested. The r1 correction kept these guards. (2) Through the open side we see palms and a distant hill fort, not the sea of 4.5 and 5.x. The fort reads as Indian, not European. (3) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small gold drop, not a flush stud. This is noted only, since the author has not yet decided which is canonical. v01 is still unacceptable: dais, turbaned courtiers in stitched shirts.

v02 fixes everything r1 flagged. The foreground figures are gone, the open side on screen right shows only the Kerala coast (palms, beach, sea, hills), and the gunners in the stain wear buff coats and steel morions with no red and no flag. The soft, smoky stain at upper left holds the thick bastion with a cannonball skipping off in stone dust. The face is on model (curled moustache, clean chin), the shirt is the collarless cream one, the raised bandaged hand shapes the wall, and the brass lamp has an open wick. The top sky is clear for the caption and the balloon. It fails on costume. Nagoji wears a broad rust-red sash at his waist. That is the commander look's signature piece and is not part of the chapter 6 bible row (village dhoti and simple cream shirt only). The sash also breaks continuity: he wears none in 4.2 and 4.4 on this page, nor in the accepted 3.3, 3.4 or 5.4. The r1 rejection of 9.1 treated a red sash as commander-look leakage. Smaller points: the r2 prompt asked for his hair tied back but it is loose. The bible allows loose hair and it matches 4.4, so keep it. The ear ornament is a small gold drop, noted only. v01 is still unacceptable: two extra foreground figures and a European town through the open side.
decisions.correction: EDIT the attached v02 image. Keep everything exactly as it is: Nagoji's face, curled moustache, clean chin, loose curly hair and ear ornament. Keep his cross-legged pose on the woven mat, the raised bandaged hand shaping a low wall in the air, the other bandaged hand resting on his knee, and the collarless long-sleeved cream shirt. Keep the laterite wall, the carved dark timber pillar and tiled eave, and the Kerala coast with palms, beach and sea through the open side on screen right. Keep the brass open-wick lamp, the soft borderless smoky stain at upper left with the low Portuguese bastion, the buff-coated gunners in morions and the cannonball skipping off its slope in stone dust, and the clear sky across the top. Change only his waist: remove the rust-red sash completely. The collarless cream shirt hangs straight down over a plain cream cotton dhoti. There is no red, rust, maroon or other coloured cloth, sash, cummerbund, belt or waistband anywhere on him, matching panels 4.2 and 4.4, where he wears only the cream shirt and the dhoti. The red sash belongs to his later commander look and must not appear in chapter 6.

decisions.issues: v02 honours the correction. The padre's cassock is black to the throat, with a plain black standing collar and no white tab or edge. The stain holds only the stocky, dark-bearded padre with the cross held high and the column of musketeers. The musketeers wear broad tilted plumed hats and buff leather coats and carry matchlocks, with no red or blue, no flags and no buildings, against plain sepia haze. The haze is soft and borderless. Nagoji sits cross-legged on the woven mat at lower left, in normal colour, talking. He has a curled moustache and clean chin, is bare-headed with loose curly hair, and wears a collarless cream shirt and dhoti with bandaged hands. Only a thin brown waist cord shows, no red sash. Varma's hand with the gold bead bracelet grips the dark spear shaft at the right foreground edge, with his head out of frame. The brass lamp has an open wick. There is no text. The pale haze at the upper right and upper centre is clear for both of Nagoji's balloons. Minor points: (1) The hall's open side and sea show at screen left, behind the pillar. Neighbours 4.2 and 4.3 put the open side on screen right. The stain dominates, so this barely reads. (2) Varma's forearm and a sliver of his gold-bordered cloth are in frame, not only the hand. He grips rather than taps. The r1 correction kept both. (3) Nagoji is medium-small rather than tiny. (4) The ear ornament is a small gold drop, noted only. v01 is still unacceptable: white collar edge on the cassock, and a church and town in the stain.

v02 fixes the round-1 fault and is acceptable. The hall is in bright daylight with carved dark pillars, a polished floor and a brass standing lamp with open wicks. The open side on screen right shows a sunlit sea and palms under a blue sky, with no storeroom clutter. One background guard stands at the left, bare-chested in a white mundu with a red sash, crossed leather belts, a topknot and a spear. The night stain bleeds softly into the hall behind Nagoji with no frame. It shows the view between a black horse's ears down a moonlit quay, with sails on the water and a burning warehouse. There are no flags, crosses, signboards or lettering in it. Nagoji matches the sheet: eyes closed, thick curled moustache, clean chin, bandaged hands, collarless cream shirt and dhoti, bare-headed with his hair loose. Minor notes: (1) His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop rather than a flush stud (noted only, as the author has not decided). (2) He wears a twisted rust-red cloth at the waist. The 5.1 prompt does not forbid it and 4.3 v02 shows the same thing, but 5.2 and 5.4 have no sash, so a later touch-up could remove it for consistency on the page. The caption fits in the upper-right sky or in the dark night sky at the top of the stain. v01 is still unacceptable: the real hall is at night and full of storeroom clutter.

v02 is acceptable. It shows the Travancore coastal hall: dark carved timber pillars, a tiled roof edge, a polished floor, a brass open-wick lamp, and a sunlit sea and palms through the open side on screen right. Two Nair guards stand in the background, bare-chested in white mundus with red sashes, crossed leather belts and topknots, holding spears. This matches the guard in 5.1. There are no European figures, rings or chairs. The only foreground element is a soft, out-of-focus bare brown shoulder with a cream-and-gold cloth at the lower left, with no face and no beard. It is larger than a sliver but reads clearly as the king. Nagoji is on model: eyes open toward the king, thick curled moustache, clean chin, collarless cream shirt and dhoti, bandaged hands. His hands and anatomy are sound. There is clear sky above his head and a wide clear sky at upper right for both balloons. Note only: his ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a flush stud. v01 is still unacceptable (a Portuguese court with morion-helmeted soldiers and a ruffed grandee).

v02 removes the bearded throne king from v01 and replaces him with a soft bare shoulder in cream and gold with a gold armlet, which is correct. Nagoji is very good: a level open-hand gesture, eyes toward the king, collarless cream shirt, dhoti, bandaged hands, clean chin, thick moustache. But the edit kept an unscripted courtier that round 1 missed. A heavyset man sits on a wooden chair in the middle ground between the king's shoulder and Nagoji. He has long loose hair, a moustache and many gold necklaces, and wears a cream robe with red-and-gold borders that covers his chest. This breaks the chapter's courtier rule (bare-chested, white mundu, topknot), the same fault that sank 4.2. He also adds a figure the script does not name. With Ramayyan off-panel and the line 'speaking to the king and not to the diwan', a jewelled seated official in view muddles who the king and the diwan are. Two smaller faults: the background guards wear white turbans and long-sleeved white tunics, unlike the bare-chested topknotted Nair guards in 5.1 and 5.2, and a walled hilltop fort sits on the headland at upper right, which the setting anchor forbids. v01 still has the bearded robed king on the red throne and the same seated courtier, so it is also unacceptable. Note only: Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop.
decisions.correction: Edit the attached v02 image. Keep everything that is right exactly as drawn: Nagoji seated cross-legged on his woven mat (his face, curly hair, thick curled moustache, clean chin, his open bandaged hand in its level gesture, the collarless cream shirt and dhoti); the soft, out-of-focus bare brown shoulder with the cream-and-gold cloth and gold armlet at the left edge; the carved stone pillars, the balustrade, the brass standing lamp with open wicks, the sunlit sea, the palms and the sky. Change only these three things. (1) Remove the heavyset seated man with long loose hair, gold necklaces and the cream robe with red-and-gold borders, together with his wooden chair, from the middle ground between the king's shoulder and Nagoji. Paint the carved pillar base and empty polished floor in their place. No other seated figure, courtier or official appears anywhere. (2) Redraw the two standing background guards to match panels 5.1 and 5.2: bare-chested Nair guards with black hair in a topknot, a white mundu, a dark red waist sash and crossed leather belts over the bare chest, each holding a spear upright. No turbans and no long-sleeved tunics. (3) Replace the walled hilltop fort on the headland at upper right with a plain green, palm-covered headland, with no fort, walls or towers anywhere. Keep the sky in the upper middle and upper right clear and low in detail for three balloons, and draw no balloons, boxes or text.

decisions.issues: v02 (the correction) is clean and follows the script and the chapter 6 bible row. The setting is the Travancore coastal hall: dark carved pillars, laterite wall, tiled rafters, and the open sea side on screen right. Bare-chested courtiers in white mundu with topknots sit behind him, Nair spear guards wear dark sashes, and the brass lamps have open wicks. The foreground is only the dark carved platform edge and a gold-bordered cream hem. Nagoji is bare-headed in a collarless cream shirt and dhoti, with his jaw set and his eyes level on the platform. His clean bandaged hands grip the cloth on his knees, sleeves down to the bandages, and the hand anatomy is sound. Upper left and upper centre are plain wall, with room for all three lettering areas. Minor notes, none a reason to reject: (1) The ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud. This matches the sheet, and the author has not yet decided which is canonical. (2) There is faint light stubble on the chin, within the bible's 'light stubble at most'. (3) His hair is loose, not tied back as the correction asked. The bible allows loose, and it matches 6.1. (4) A tiny, hazy fortified headland sits on the far horizon at right. It is too small to read as European and matches the distant headland already seen in 6.1. v01 is not acceptable: it is a Portuguese/Goa setting with helmeted, breastplated European soldiers, a seated official in an embroidered coat, an iron wall ring and a European desk.

v02 (the round-2 correction) is acceptable. Ibrahim matches his sheet: white turban, grey-flecked beard, muted-teal short coat over a cream vest with bulging pockets, white mundu, blue-striped shoulder cloth and sandals. Both hands are spread and drawn soundly. The setting is a Kerala hall with dark carved wooden pillars, a brass lamp with open wicks, woven mats and a polished floor. The open side is on screen right, showing the sea, moored native boats and the red laterite wall, which matches 7.3. The one distant guard is correct: bare-chested, white mundu, crossed belts, plain spear, topknot. There are no Europeans and no text. Upper-left and upper-right sky are clear for both balloons. Minor notes: (1) The scar is on his left cheek (screen right) as required, but it is a faintly reddish line, not fully pale; this matches the sheet. (2) The hall also opens to sky and palms behind the guard on screen left. (3) Panel 6.4 shows stone pillars where 7.1 and 7.3 show dark timber; this is a page-to-page inconsistency in 6.4, not here. (4) Ibrahim looks slightly off-camera toward screen left, presumably at the platform just out of frame. v01 stays rejected: it shows Portuguese/European figures (velvet-robed nobleman, black-gowned cleric, morion-helmeted soldiers with halberds) and a European chair and table.

v02 is clean and follows the correction. The camera is behind Varma's shoulder and the open side is on screen right. Varma wears the formal cream-and-gold turban with a peacock crest, has a bare back and sits on a dark carved wooden seat. The courtiers sit bare-chested in white mundu with topknots, and the guards wear white cotton with dark sashes. The boats in the inlet are local and the lamps are open brass. Nagoji has a curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin, a collarless cream shirt, a dhoti and bandages over his palms and knuckles. Large clear sky at upper right takes both balloons. Notes only: (1) Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud; the author has not decided. (2) His hair is loose, not tied back as the pre-generation note asked; the bible allows either. (3) The red laterite outer wall at right has a rounded corner, but it reads as Kerala laterite, not a European bastion. (4) From behind, Varma's black hair hangs loose and curly. v01 is rejected: European morion soldiers, a European castle and a red-velvet gilded throne.

v02 fixes every round-1 fault. The inner wall is closed plaster with dark carved pillars, with no sea, sky or ships. There is no red sash, only a plain cream dhoti, and no European soldiers. The empty dark wooden platform with open brass lamps is at screen left. Nagoji sits in profile at screen right, leaning in with one bandaged hand reaching out. Bandages cover his palms and knuckles, his chin is clean-shaven and he wears a collarless cream shirt. The background courtiers and guards are small, bare-chested, in white mundu with topknots and dark sashes. Dark rafters across the top leave room for two balloons. Notes only: (1) His near (left) sleeve is pushed up to the elbow, though the pre-generation note wanted it down to the wrist. Only the outer forearm shows (back of the hand toward camera), so the inner-forearm brand is not involved. (2) His hair is loose; the bible allows it. (3) His ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a stud; the author has not decided. v01 is rejected: sea visible behind him, red sash and European morion soldiers.

v02 carries out the edit cleanly. The large foreground turbaned figure is gone, and Varma is the only person in frame. He matches his sheet: namam mark, curled moustache, pearl earrings, cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock crest, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth and gold necklaces. He looks steadily toward the right edge. The spear butt taps the mat with two small motion ticks. The open side is at screen left, with a kingfisher on the parapet and waves on the sand. The silver-conch-on-red banner carries no lettering, the lamps are open brass, and only the edge of Nagoji's mat shows at lower right. The plain wall right of his head takes the balloon. Minor consistency notes: (1) The hall floor here is polished stone tile, while 8.1 and 8.4 show woven mats on dark wood. (2) The view outside is open surf beach, not the inlet with boats seen in 8.1, though the script asks for waves on sand. (3) The seat has carved lion-head armrests, which reads as an Indian simhasana, not a European throne. v01 is rejected for the second turbaned, crested figure in the right foreground.

v02 is clean and honours the review correction. Ramayyan sits alone at his low table on the raised timber platform. He matches the sheet: thin, curly receding hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery. He turns down toward screen right with an open gesturing hand, and the man on the mat stays out of frame. The props are an open-wick brass lamp with no glass, a brass ink pot and tied palm-leaf bundles with no script, plus a spear rack. Through the opening there is only an inlet, local boats, palms and a red laterite wall: no church, no Europeans and no helmets. Minor continuity note: the open sea side shows behind him and to the right, whereas 9.2 and 9.5 put the open side on screen left. It is the same coastal hall with dark carved pillars and a tiled roof, so this is accepted. Lettering fits in the open sky left of his head (x 0.08 to 0.32, y 0.02 to 0.40) and between the right pillars under the roof (x 0.68 to 0.86, y 0.20 to 0.33). v01 stays rejected: a turbaned, sashed and bearded foreground figure, helmeted guards and a European church and fort.

v02 is a clean edit that honours the correction. It is a tight head-and-shoulders shot of Ramayyan alone, with a faint amused smile and sharp eyes turned toward screen right. He matches the sheet: curly receding hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery. His stylus and the tied palm-leaf ledger match the sheet's detail panels and carry no writing. Both hands are sound. There is no foreground figure, chain or collar. The right two thirds is plain plastered wall (x 0.55 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.60), which leaves ample room for both lettering lines. Minor note: the background is a stone pillar and a plaster wall, not the dark carved timber of 9.1. This was kept from v01 at the edit's request, and it is consistent with the plastered upper wall in 9.2. v01 stays rejected: it has a chained, shackled figure in the foreground.

v02 honours the review correction: no Europeans. Only a sliver of Varma shows at the near left (back of the cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare shoulder, pearls), on a gilded lion-armrest seat beside an open-wick brass lamp. Two bare-chested Travancore guards with crossed belts and topknots stand by the dark carved pillars. Nagoji matches his sheet (thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, bare-headed, cream collarless shirt, dhoti, both hands bandaged, barefoot), and the open side of the hall is on screen right with clear sky at upper right for the balloon. Minor notes: his ear ornament is a small hanging drop, not a stud (author undecided, not a reason to reject). His hair is loose rather than tied back, which the bible allows. His sleeves are rolled to the forearm rather than reaching the bandaged wrists. A small hazy laterite fort sits on the far headland, which matches 10.3 and 10.5. v01 is unacceptable: it has a European in a ruff on a European chair and Portuguese morion soldiers.

v02 honours the edit: the foreground over-the-shoulder figure and his second crest are gone. This is now a clean two-shot. Varma matches the varma-v1 sheet: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest (correct for the formal audience), the sheet's forehead mark, pearl necklaces, armlets and spear, with his gaze lowered to screen left toward the man below. Ramayyan sits at the king's left hand (screen right) and matches his sheet: thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery, palm-leaf bundle and stylus, and no writing on the ola. The open side of the hall is on screen left. Clear sky at upper left, plain wall at upper right and bare floor at lower left leave room for three balloons. Minor notes: Ramayyan's lips are closed and he holds the stylus as if writing, so the quiet translating is carried by his turned head and the lettering. This hall shows pale stone pillars and a turned-baluster railing, lighter than the dark carved pillars of 10.1 and 9.5, but 9.4 also has a balustrade, so this is acceptable. v01 is unacceptable: it still has the foreground figure wearing a second turban and crest.

v02 fixed Nagoji as asked: both of his hands are now bandaged. His right hand rests at his right hip, his head is turned to screen right up the coastline, he is bare-headed in the cream shirt and dhoti, barefoot, with no sword or sash. But the edit leaked the bandage onto Ramayyan: his LEFT hand and wrist (the arm hanging at his side, on screen left of his body, at lower left) is now wrapped in the same white bandage. Ramayyan is uninjured and his sheet has bare hands, so this is a continuity error a reader will notice. v01 is still unacceptable: Nagoji's left hand is unbandaged. Minor notes for both candidates, not reasons to reject: the building at the upper-left edge has a pointed-arch window under a Kerala tiled roof. The far headland fort has one slender tall tower. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small drop (author undecided). His hair is loose, which the bible allows.
